info.title: Scratchpad Engine API
info.description:
Multi-platform automation API for Chrome (CDP) and Android (ADB).

Every error response — over HTTP, WebSocket, or MCP — uses the same typed `ErrorResponse` envelope (fields: `type`, `message`, `code`, `hint`, `request_id`). The `request_id` is generated by the request-id middleware, echoed back in the `X-Request-ID` response header, and repeated in every error envelope so one failure is traceable end to end.

**Honest scope note:** the REST surface is currently a subset of the WebSocket/MCP surface. `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/actions` validates and documents six action types (`navigate`, `observe`, `click`, `type`, `scroll`, `wait`). A raw `protocol.ActionRequest` body is also passed through to the engine, but full ActionRequest parity over REST is a later milestone. See the WebSocket endpoints and the `ActionRequest` schema for the full engine action surface.

get.description: Reports process readiness as JSON with per-engine session counts and uptime. Always 200 when the process is up.
Reports the server build version, Go runtime version, and module path.
Exposes process metrics in Prometheus text exposition format: action counters by type, observe-latency histogram, session churn, and error counts by code.

text/plain.example:
# HELP scratchpad_actions_total Actions executed by type.
# TYPE scratchpad_actions_total counter
scratchpad_actions_total{action="click"} 12

post.description: Creates a new engine session. The request body is optional; an empty body creates a headful Chrome session. Send `platform: "android"` or `kind: "android"` to create an Android (ADB) session.

500.description: Session creation failed (e.g. Chrome binary not found or ADB device unavailable)

example.hint: Check CHROME_PATH or install Google Chrome, then retry.

delete.description: Closes the session's engine and removes it from the manager. Deleting a missing session returns a 404 ErrorResponse.

example.hint: List active sessions via /healthz, then retry with a valid session id.

post.description:
Executes an action against a session and returns the resulting observation.

The body may be one of three shapes:
1. **Typed envelope** — `{"action": {"type": "navigate|observe|click|type|scroll|wait", ...}}` (the validated, documented REST surface).
2. **Raw InitializeRequest** — `{"url": "https://...", "viewport": {...}}` navigates the session.
3. **Raw protocol.ActionRequest** — `{"action": "hover", "selector": {...}}` is passed straight through to the engine. This works for the full action surface, but it is undocumented pass-through behavior: parity is a later milestone.

Every success returns an ObservationResponse (a `delta` when the tree changed by less than a full snapshot).

400.description: Malformed body or unsupported action type

example.hint: Send one of: navigate, observe, click, type, scroll, wait.

get.description: Lists the built-in device-emulation presets (name, viewport, pixel ratio, mobile/touch flags). Pass a name as `device` when creating a session to start it pre-emulated as that device.

post.description: Turns network interception on/off and installs mock/abort/continue routes for a Chrome session (item 14). Adding a route implicitly enables interception; response bodies of intercepted requests are captured for network_response_body assertions.

get.description: Returns and clears the requests recorded since the last call (url, method, status, duration, response body when interception captured it). Aborted (blocked) requests report status -1.

400.description: Engine does not support network interception (e.g. Android)

get.description: Returns the captured network traffic as a HAR archive (Chrome engine only). Served as an attachment.

400.description: Engine does not support HAR (e.g. Android)

get.description: Returns the current page DOM as an HTML attachment (Chrome engine only).

400.description: Engine does not support DOM export

get.description: Returns the session's console-log ring buffer (newest entries last).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of log entries to return. Default 200; 0 returns the whole ring buffer.

get.description: Captures a screenshot of the current page or screen. Chrome supports jpeg/png/webp and full-page capture; Android returns an error.

parameters.name: fullPage
parameters.description: Capture the full scrollable page instead of the viewport.

parameters.name: element
parameters.description: CSS selector of an element to crop the capture to.

400.description: Screenshot not supported for this engine

get.summary: Fetch a captured artifact (e.g. a PDF)
get.description: Serves a binary artifact produced by the session (such as a `capture_pdf` output) by its base name. Only files the engine itself produced are reachable.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Base name of the artifact, e.g. `receipt.pdf`.

400.description: Artifacts not supported for this engine

post.summary: Compare the current screenshot to a baseline
post.description: Runs a `screenshot_matches` assertion against the provided baseline image and returns the assertion result (perceptual dHash comparison).

400.description: Missing expected_base64, malformed body, or the assertion failed

post.description: Starts screen/video recording for the session (Chrome engine). The engine writes a webm file; the returned outputPath is where it will land.

400.description: Recording not supported for this engine

post.description: Stops recording and returns the webm bytes. The path where the recording was written is echoed in the `X-Output-Path` response header.

X-Output-Path.description: Path where the recording was written on the server.

400.description: Recording not supported for this engine

post.description: Starts a Chrome DevTools Protocol trace for the session.

400.description: Tracing not supported for this engine

post.description: Stops tracing and returns the gzipped trace JSON. The path where the trace was written is echoed in the `X-Output-Path` response header.

X-Output-Path.description: Path where the trace was written on the server.

400.description: Tracing not supported for this engine

get.description:
Upgrades to a WebSocket connection driving a dedicated Chrome engine session.

After the upgrade the server sends `{"sessionId": "..."}`, then the client sends typed protocol envelopes and receives ObservationResponse or ErrorResponse messages. This transport carries the FULL engine action surface, unlike the REST actions endpoint.

Client message envelope: `{"type": "navigate|observe|action|resize", "data": {...}}` — see `WebSocketEnvelope`.
Upgrades to a WebSocket connection driving a dedicated Android (ADB) session. Same envelope protocol as /ws.

headless.description: Run Chrome headless. Default false. Ignored for Android.

ErrorResponse.description: Typed error envelope used by every transport (HTTP, WebSocket, MCP). Carries a stable machine code, a human hint, and the request id for correlation.

request_id.description: Correlation id stamped by the request-id middleware. Echo it back via the X-Request-ID header to correlate retries.

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code (e.g. selector_no_match, timeout).

type.description: Severity: fatal = session is broken, action = this action failed but can retry, warning = succeeded with issues.

action.description: The action that was being attempted (empty for session-level errors).

selector.description: The selector that failed, when applicable.

screenshot.description: Base64 JPEG captured at the moment of failure (WebSocket path).

hint.description: What the agent should try next.

Selector.description: Structured locator. Resolution order: CSS > XPath > text > role > test_id > placeholder. Pass multiple strategies and the best match wins.

InitializeRequest.description: Navigates the session to a URL. Also accepted directly as the body of POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/actions.

ActionEnvelope.description: The typed action envelope accepted by the REST actions endpoint.

ActionPayload.description: The typed action payload validated by the REST API. Only six actions are supported today: navigate, observe, click, type, scroll, wait. Full ActionRequest parity over REST is a later milestone.

url.description: navigate: URL to open (http://... or an Android package name).

ActionRequest.description: Full protocol ActionRequest (the WebSocket/MCP action surface). Over REST it is accepted in raw form and passed through to the engine — the full surface works, but only the six actions in ActionPayload are validated and documented today; parity is a later milestone.

pattern.description: Regex/text pattern for waits and assertions.

AssertionRequest.description: Web-first assertion: the engine polls until the condition holds or the retry timeout elapses.

type.description: element_exists, element_visible, element_checked, element_count, text_equals, text_contains, text_matches, attr_equals, attr_contains, attr_matches, value_equals, page_title, page_url, url_matches, console_error_count, network_request_status, network_request_count, network_no_errors, network_response_body, screenshot_matches.

ObservationResponse.description: Snapshot of the current page/screen returned after every action and observation. When the tree changed by less than a full snapshot, `type` is "delta" and `delta` carries the change instead of a full `spatial_tree`.

SpatialNode.description: A UI element in the accessibility tree.

interactive.description: True for actionable elements (buttons, links, inputs).

value.description: Current value of a form control.

ActionResult.description: Rich feedback returned after every action.

screenshot.description: Base64 JPEG captured after the action.

element_highlight.description: Base64 JPEG with the targeted element outlined.

attempts.description: How many times the assertion was polled before resolving.

NetworkRoute.description: A mock/abort/continue interception rule. pattern is a CDP-style glob ("*" any sequence, "?" any one char); add a trailing "*" to also match query strings.

status.description: HTTP status for a mocked response.

body_base64.description: Base64-encoded body for a mocked response.

enable.description: Explicit toggle: true enables interception, false disables it and clears routes/bodies.

NetworkRequestInfo.description: One recorded network request. Aborted (blocked) requests report status -1.

response_body.description: Captured body when interception was active for the request.

WebSocketEnvelope.description: Typed envelope for agent-to-engine WebSocket messages.

data.description: Payload; shape depends on type: InitializeRequest for navigate, ActionRequest for action, ResizeRequest for resize, DeviceListResponse for devices, NetworkListResponse for network_list, absent for observe and network_enable/network_disable.

WebSocketHandshake.description: First message sent by the server immediately after the upgrade.
